Old raw lines 84-102 and new raw lines 130-164 describe required bank-authorized mandates. Stripe automatically configures a one-off mandate with fixed payment amount, ad hoc cadence and one payment, and the inferred purpose can be overridden. A recurring merchant specifies the least permissive terms; fixed amount requires an amount and payment equality, maximum defaults apply, and dated bank caps still matter. New raw lines 134-150 clarify the customer authorizes at their bank, the merchant need not present its own legal mandate text for this method, and PaymentMethod detachment cancels the mandate while customer bank revocation is another path.

Old raw lines 104-114 and new raw lines 93-128 cover full and partial refunds within two years, typically minutes with bank-dependent delays, and final disputes. November specifically says billing name must match the bank-account name for refunds of PayID payments, since mismatch can cause failure, and clarifies full disputes only, no evidence or appeal, Stripe balance deduction and two dispute webhooks. To return funds after resolving with the customer, the customer makes a new payment. Use refund status for outcome.

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw `raw/stripe-payments-payto-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw `raw/stripe-payto-2025.md`. Current summaries `wiki/sources/source-stripe-payto.md`.

- Q1. For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payto`, what documented behavior, prerequisites, actors and state transitions does the complete new capture establish? How do these compare with the matched prior capture and each mapped summary?

- Q2. Which changes are substantive, presentational or navigation-only? Identify the exact dated qualifications, conflicts and reciprocal routes that the proposed disposition should preserve.

reviewed_answers.Q1: The 2026-11-07 overview at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payto documents approved, domestic Australian AUD payments using PayID or a BSB and account number. New raw lines 9-190 and 245-273 show identity verification, customer-bank mandate authorization, Stripe's typically delayed final result within 60 seconds of authorization, one-off automatic mandates, restricted recurring terms, and separate settlement. The ordinary account limit is AUD 10,000, with approved higher limits to AUD 100,000 and separate bank mandate caps. Old raw lines 8-180 already cover the core flow, historical dispute finality, refunds and bank caps. November adds PayID refund-name matching, cancellation by PaymentMethod detachment or customer bank revocation, and destination-charge statement identity. source-stripe-payto.md preserves the older flow but overstates timing and one-off mandate defaults and omits the new operational qualifications.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payto, old raw lines 8-180 and new raw lines 9-273 preserve the dated AU mandate, verification, typically delayed result and final-dispute behavior. New limits, approval and MCC detail, refund and mandate conditions, and Connect statement identity are substantive. The reordered sections, bank link labels and separate variant links are presentational or navigation changes. Preserve the new recurring and Setup Intent support alongside the off-session unsupported cell and the separate matrix's future-usage footnote. Correct the reciprocal Express Checkout Element and exclusivity claims using the dated product and UPI matrices. Retain May's listed Connect charge types and the 43-institution bank tables, including the AUD 25,000 mandate thresholds and separate Westpac high-risk payment limit while adding the full November raw to source-stripe-payto.md and maintaining the Stripe index and Real-Time Payments concept routes.
